Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Compression Reduces 12G-SDI Latency by 30% in Live Graphics Transport

BluBlu Studios recently announced the successful integration of JPEG XS compression into their live graphics transport workflow, leveraging the technology to reduce latency in 12G-SDI signals. This development is particularly significant for live broadcast applications where real-time signal transport and frame-accuracy are crucial. The implementation involves the use of JPEG XS compression to minimize the bitrate required for transporting high-resolution graphics over 12G-SDI, thereby reducing the latency associated with signal transmission.

Operational ROI

The introduction of JPEG XS compression into live graphics transport workflows offers significant operational benefits, particularly in terms of reduced transmission cost and lower latency compared to traditional methods such as satellite or fibre transmission. By minimizing the bitrate required for signal transport, broadcast CTOs can achieve cost savings on transmission infrastructure and reduce the complexity of signal routing. This directly affects the workflow step of signal transmission, where reduced latency and lower costs can enhance the overall efficiency of live broadcast operations. Quantitatively, the reduction in latency by 30% can translate into improved real-time responsiveness and better synchronization of graphics with live video feeds.

In comparison to existing approaches, the use of JPEG XS compression simplifies signal routing by reducing the number of signals that need to be transported, thus decreasing the hardware rack footprint required for signal processing and transmission. This operational change can lead to reduced power consumption, lower maintenance costs, and an overall more streamlined broadcast infrastructure. Additionally, the lower latency achieved through JPEG XS compression can enable more responsive and interactive live broadcast experiences, such as real-time graphics updates and audience participation.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live graphics transport workflows must consider cybersecurity implications and compliance with relevant broadcast standards. The use of JPEG XS, which is compliant with standards such as SMPTE ST 2110, ensures that the compressed signals can be seamlessly integrated into existing IP-based broadcast infrastructures. Furthermore, adherence to standards like NMOS IS-04 for device discovery and registration facilitates the secure and efficient connection of devices within the broadcast network. The compressed signals can also be transported over secure protocols like SRT or RIST, ensuring the integrity and authenticity of the signals during transmission.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of JPEG XS compression in live graphics transport requires compatible hardware capable of encoding and decoding JPEG XS compressed signals, such as graphics cards or dedicated encoding devices, and a network infrastructure that can support the required bandwidth for transporting the compressed signals.
  • Compatibility: Compliance with standards such as SMPTE ST 2110-20 for professional media over managed IP networks and NMOS IS-04 for device discovery and registration is essential for ensuring seamless integration and secure operation within the broadcast infrastructure.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the upcoming updates to the JPEG XS standard, which may include enhancements for even higher compression ratios or improved support for emerging broadcast technologies like 8K resolution, to stay ahead of the curve in live graphics transport and signal compression.

The successful integration of JPEG XS compression into live graphics transport workflows signals a significant step forward in reducing latency and improving the efficiency of live broadcast operations. Engineering teams should prioritize the evaluation and adoption of JPEG XS compression technology to enhance their live graphics transport capabilities and stay competitive in the evolving broadcast landscape.

Analysis: ST 2110 adoption enables BluBlu Studios to process Death Howl's launch trailer with precise timing and low latency, utilizing NMOS for device discovery and connection, optimizing the 4K video workflow with H.264 codec at 50Mbps bitrate.
